core-3.first_prompt:
Last session you sketched these options:
- Whole-visit revisions: keep each submitted visit intact and send competing revisions to review. The tablets track base revision IDs, and the review/export side needs a revision comparison screen and holds unresolved visits out of the CSV.
- Field-aware three-way merge: automatically combine unrelated field edits and review overlaps. The tablets keep base snapshots and send structured changes, and review/export needs field-level provenance plus maintained merge rules.

Let's go with whole-visit revisions. I'll take a bigger review queue over maintaining merge rules that can combine scientifically related edits without noticing. Go ahead and finish the record-store design; we'll do tablet sync and review/export after that.
first_turn_assertions: By the end of the run, docs/intent/record-store/record-store-design.md makes whole-visit revisions the concurrency policy, replacing the open-choice placeholder. A run whose first turn stops at an earlier phase's review (for example an HLD stop) before reaching this design also passes if its reply names whole-visit revisions as the choice the design will carry.

The first reply offers, as a question for the user, to record the whole-visit-revisions choice as a standalone decision doc (a phrasing like 'want me to write this up as a decision doc?' or a stated default such as 'I recorded it as a row; say so and I'll write a full decision doc' both count). The offer is made once, not repeated across the reply.

The reply makes the offer and presents a Decisions & Alternatives row in the record-store design as the alternative to the doc, either by naming it as the lighter option or by having already added one that the doc would expand. A reply that makes no offer fails.
The first turn creates no file under any `decisions/` directory (check `changes1.patch`) and writes no standalone decision-doc content into another file.
core-3.follow_up_prompt: Yeah, write that up properly, including why we'd still consider the other approach and what the tablet and export work will have to accommodate.
follow_up_assertions: The decision doc first appears in the follow-up turn (absent from `changes1.patch`, present in `changes.patch`), in `docs/intent/record-store/decisions/` (the owning node's directory, since record-store owns the choice), named for the decision rather than numbered. A doc placed in the project-level `docs/decisions/` fails.

The decision doc lays out both options (whole-visit revisions, field-aware three-way merge) against more than one criterion, states the choice, and states the accepted cost (a larger coordinator review queue, including review work for unrelated-field edits). It carries no EARS spec IDs and no `status` field.
The record-store design's Decisions & Alternatives table has a row for the concurrency policy that links to the decision doc's path.
The decision doc is written to be read cold: it does not narrate the session (no 'last session', 'you sketched', 'the user chose', or 'we discussed').
